8ba3bcb143b805a8.description: Multiple sclerosis (MS) prevalence has increased to medium-to-high levels in several countries of the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), while Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) exposure as one of the most consistently reported MS risk factors is common throughout the region. This systematic review and meta-analysis descriptively mapped published estimates of MS prevalence and EBV seroprevalence alongside each other in MENA countries. We searched MEDLINE, PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science until 18 June 2022. Observational studies reporting MS prevalence or EBV seroprevalence among healthy MENA populations were eligible. For quantitative EBV synthesis, we restricted analyses to studies reporting VCA-IgG seroprevalence to improve comparability across studies. Studies reporting the prevalence of specific type of MS or those assessing EBV infection by IgA antibodies or non-serological tissues or without a control arm representing general population were excluded. The Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools were used to determine the quality of the studies. The heterogeneity of studies was evaluated using I 2 statistics. 8ba3bcb143b805a8.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 131 studies in the Middle East and North Africa found pooled MS prevalence of 51.02 per 100,000 and EBV VCA-IgG seroprevalence of 75%. Pooled MS prevalence rose over time, from 12 per 100,000 in the earliest period.

f5815cad7cae3e07.description: Background Tolebrutinib is an oral, brain-penetrant Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor being investigated for multiple sclerosis (MS). Early data point to reduced relapse rates and radiological disease activity, along with a reassuring safety profile.
